With `"auto"` a job that finishes within the synchronous time limit still answers 200 with the plan, exactly as without it; a job that would outgrow the limit answers **202** with a `jobId` instead, keeps solving, and its plan is read with `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` (the same poll as engine `max`). The call is billed once, when the plan is written; a solve that fails is not billed. Without this field such a job answers 504 `solve_timeout` with the `jobId` in `details` and is not charged. The official SDKs send it and wait

changed.words: +Use it for "how efficient is this home", "what would it cost to heat" and "what should I upgrade", when an `akey` is known (from search_addresses or any row another tool returned). address_report carries the same certificate among its nine parts; house_age gives only the build era. A home with no certificate returns `certificate: false` and a `reason` (one not sold or let since 2008 may never have had one); that is missing evidence, not a bad rating. Check `certificate_year`: an old certificate may predate later work on the home.

+Use it for those yes/no facts about a home you already have an `akey` for (from search_addresses or any row another tool returned). For prices, energy, the street and the area use address_report (everything) or the single-topic tools. Never guess an `akey`: an unknown one fails with "address not found". A field that is null means no public record, not "no": `owner_occupied` null is not the same as false.

+Use it for "when was this house built" and "what is it built like" (solid walls, cavity walls, asbestos era). It takes the address as text, so no `akey` is needed; for the full energy picture of one home use energy_performance. Matching is by text: when `fuzzy` is true the rows are near matches, not the address asked for, so say so or search_addresses for the exact home. `band` null means that home has no certificate with an age band; `first_yr` is the first sale since 1995, not the build year.

+Use it for "is this price fair" or "what might this home be worth" on one home with an `akey` (from search_addresses or any row another tool returned). For a home on the market, negotiation_brief adds the asking-price cuts and time on the market. When the home has no floor area on record, or its district too few sales of its type, the answer has `comparable: false` and a `reason` naming the tool to use instead; pass that on rather than inventing a figure.

+Use it for "is a leasehold flat cheaper here", "what is an A-rated house worth over a D", "do bigger homes cost less per m2". For several districts use compare_areas; for one home use price_check. When a district has too few sales of that type the tool fails and names the property types it does have, so ask again with one of those.

+Use it for "what do homes on this street go for per square metre". To judge one price or an asking price use price_check, which sets the street beside the district; for a list of the sales themselves use recent_sales with the street as `area`; for a whole district use area_overview. Takes an `akey` from search_addresses or any row another tool returned. A street with no sale that has a floor area on record returns an empty `years`; that means too little evidence, not a price of zero.

+Use it for amenities and transport. Crime and air quality are in address_report; compare_homes also names the nearest station, school, supermarket and park for two to four homes. Keys come from search_addresses or any row another tool returned. A kind with nothing inside the radius is left out of `kinds` (an empty `kinds` means nothing within it at all): widen `radius_m` or use `closest`. Schools here are by distance only, not catchment or Ofsted rating.
